items.title: Google launches more visible links in AI Overviews and AI Mode
items.summary: Google is rolling out more visible links in AI Overviews and AI Mode, where links appear as pop-up cards on hover in desktop views and show more prominent details about websites. This update, previously tested, aims to make it easier to access web content and is expected to increase user engagement with links. The change has implications for SEO by potentially driving more traffic to websites through AI-driven search experiences, though measurement tools like Search Console are not yet available.

items.title: Why AI optimization is just long-tail SEO done right
items.summary: The article argues that AI optimization, including terms like GEO, AEO, and AIO, is essentially long-tail SEO, as LLMs rely on web search and retrieval-augmented generation to handle detailed prompts, shifting SEO focus from competitive head terms to capturing nuanced, conversational long-tail queries. It explains how brands can use LLMs to generate realistic customer questions, analyze on-site search data for content opportunities, and create authoritative, experience-driven content that builds trust and ranks across search engines like Google, Bing, and Brave. This evolution implies that SEO strategies must prioritize understanding audience needs through AI-assisted research and producing high-quality, specific content to dominate the expanding long tail in AI-driven search.

items.title: Google shifts Lookalike to AI signals in Demand Gen
items.summary: Google is updating Lookalike audiences in Demand Gen campaigns to function as AI-driven optimization signals rather than strict targeting constraints, starting March 2026, which allows the system to expand reach beyond the selected similarity tiers for potentially higher conversions and lower CPA. This change reduces advertiser control over audience delivery, aligning with broader automation trends similar to those on Meta Platforms, and introduces an opt-out option for maintaining legacy strict targeting. The shift emphasizes AI-led audience expansion, requiring marketers to test impacts on performance metrics like scale and cost efficiency.

items.title: 5 Ways New Businesses Can Show Up In ChatGPT & Gemini
items.summary: The article outlines strategies for new businesses to gain visibility in AI-generated responses from ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity, emphasizing that AI prioritizes verifiable trust signals, structured content, and external validations over company age. An experiment with a new B2B company showed initial appearances in 5% of relevant AI responses within six weeks through focused efforts on machine-readable sites, answer-first content, and early external mentions. Implications for SEO and content marketing include shifting from traditional ranking to building entity clarity, semantic structure, and authority via third-party sources to reduce AI uncertainty and improve citation rates in generative search.

items.title: Reader Critiques BookTok’s Viral Romantasy Formula After Trying Four Hits
items.summary: Nicole Sudjono explored BookTok's popular romantasy books like Fourth Wing and Alchemized, drawn in by their fantasy escapism and social media hype. She identified a repetitive formula of dark romance, simple language, toxic love interests, and heavy spice content that echoes unedited fanfiction trends. Disillusioned, she abandoned BookTok recommendations in favor of deeper classics like Eragon and The Lord of the Rings.

items.title: Mary Kubica’s 'She's the One' Debuts at #3 on Hardcover Fiction Bestsellers, Snapped Up for TV Adaptation
items.summary: Psychological thriller 'She's the One' by Mary Kubica has debuted at #3 on Publishers Weekly's hardcover fiction bestsellers list for the week of February 16, 2026. Just one day after publication, Gaumont—the studio behind Lupin and Narcos—optioned the book for a television series. This marks a major win for Kubica in the competitive thriller market.

items.title: Shannon J. Spann’s Dark YA Fantasy 'Enter Stage Left' Hits Children’s Fiction Bestsellers
items.summary: Shannon J. Spann’s 'Enter Stage Left', a propulsive YA fantasy structured like a theater script, debuted at #11 on Publishers Weekly's children’s fiction list. Drawing from the author’s theater background, it celebrates drama's allure for misfits through innovative dialogue and world-building. The book underscores ongoing trends in YA speculative fiction.

items.title: Nnedi Okorafor’s 'The Daughter Who Remains' Launches as New Fantasy Novella
items.summary: Acclaimed author Nnedi Okorafor releases 'The Daughter Who Remains', the third novella in her She Who Knows trilogy set in the Who Fears Death universe, published by Astra House/DAW on February 17, 2026. Sorcerer Najeeba returns to her origins on a perilous journey with glassmaker Dedan and camel MorningStar. This addition expands Okorafor’s influential Africanfuturist speculative world.

items.title: Téa Obreht Lands Deal for Speculative Novel 'Sunrise' Spanning a Century in a Ghost Town
items.summary: In Publishers Weekly's book deals for the week of February 16, 2026, Téa Obreht sold 'Sunrise', intertwining three lives over 100 years in a mysterious ghost town. The story centers on Nina, who crashes from a plane into an abandoned Old West settlement, uncovering a long-buried enigma. Set for August 2026 publication, it blends historical and speculative elements.

items.title: Emerald Fennell's 'Wuthering Heights' Adaptation Sparks Fan Debates and Romantasy Buzz
items.summary: Emerald Fennell directs the gothic romance adaptation of Emily Brontë’s 'Wuthering Heights,' starring Jacob Elordi as Heathcliff and Margot Robbie as Catherine Earnshaw, featuring Charli xcx's original soundtrack as a narrative element. Released around Valentine's Day 2026, the film has ignited discussions on historical accuracy, character identities, and its status as a love story amid colliding fan communities. It exemplifies the surge in romantasy trends blending literature, pop music, and film fandoms.

items.title: New 'The Pendragon Cycle: Rise of the Merlin' Series Adapts Heroic Fantasy Saga
items.summary: DailyWire+ presents 'The Pendragon Cycle: Rise of the Merlin,' adapting Stephen R. Lawhead’s first two books, Taliesin and Merlin, which reimagine Arthurian legend through Celtic myths and prophecy. Starring Tom Sharp as Merlin and Rose Reid as Princess Charis, the seven-episode season explores the fall of Atlantis, Britain's awakening, and epic destinies, drawing comparisons to 'The Lord of the Rings' for its mythic depth. Set for full 2026 release with five episodes already aired.

items.title: Ryan Gosling Stars in Highly Anticipated Sci-Fi Adaptation 'Project Hail Mary'
items.summary: Andy Weir's 'Project Hail Mary' hits screens March 10, 2026, directed by Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, with Ryan Gosling as a lone astronaut racing to save Earth from a catastrophic solar event. Featured atop lists of 2026's most awaited book-to-film projects, the sci-fi thriller echoes 'The Martian' with high-stakes space adventure and unexpected alliances. Co-starring Sandra Hüller and others, it's generating massive pre-release excitement.

items.title: Christopher Nolan's Star-Studded 'The Odyssey' Tops 2026 Fantasy Adaptations
items.summary: Christopher Nolan directs Homer's epic 'The Odyssey' for July 17, 2026 release, starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, Tom Holland as Telemachus, Zendaya as Athena, and Charlize Theron as Circe. Highlighted in recent anticipation roundups, the grand-scale fantasy adaptation promises Nolan's signature spectacle in retelling the hero's journey home. It's poised to be a major cinematic event bridging ancient myth and modern blockbuster filmmaking.

items.title: Cantwell, Moran Reintroduce Bill to Help Small Business Leverage AI Tools
items.summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026, reintroduced by Senators Cantwell and Moran, authorizes the U.S. Department of Commerce to collaborate with the Small Business Administration to develop and distribute AI training resources and tools. This enables small businesses to integrate AI for operations like financial management, marketing, and supply chain management. The legislation addresses uneven access to AI training, helping small businesses compete and grow amid rising AI adoption.
items.source: U.S. Senate Committee on Commerce, Science and Transportation

items.title: Free program teaches small business owners how to use AI
items.summary: The Bronx Chamber of Commerce and Google.org launched the free four-week AI Advantage Program, teaching small business owners to apply AI tools to marketing, customer engagement, workflow automation, data analysis, and decision-making without technical expertise. Over 100 businesses applied for the first cohort of 70, with participants noting AI frees them from busy work to focus on core activities. The program reduces AI stigma and bridges tech gaps, with more cohorts planned.

items.title: New Study Reveals Small-Business Enthusiasm for AI
items.summary: A Connected Commerce Council study shows 70% of small-business leaders have invested in or plan to adopt AI tools, with 55% reporting higher employee productivity and 53% viewing AI as critical to success. Among digital ad users, 72% find AI simplifies campaigns and boosts effectiveness. The findings underscore AI's role in saving time, cutting costs, and driving growth for SMBs.

items.title: Why Agentic AI Is Breaking The SaaS Pricing Model
items.summary: Agentic AI disrupts SaaS pricing by rendering 'seats' or user-based models obsolete, as AI agents dynamically orchestrate tasks and evolve, shifting to hybrid models blending usage metrics with customization. This challenges fixed pricing, pushing value-based relationships that reflect AI-driven outcomes. Small businesses must adapt to complex SaaS costs tied to bespoke AI configurations and services.
